records.name: Estonia
records.summary_text:
Estonia is broadly workable with a strong progressive trajectory but a social climate that lags the law. It was the first Baltic and post-Soviet country to legalise same-sex marriage (2024), approved a national LGBT+ equal-opportunities action plan in 2025 (with particular attention to trans people), joined 16 EU states in urging Hungary to revise its anti-LGBT laws, and held Tallinn Pride in 2025. There are no documented severe traveler-axis incidents — no mob violence, trans-tourist rape, police-brutality, or foreign-trans-detention case.

records.name: Lithuania
records.summary_text:
The country is broadly workable, at the lower end, with one of Europe's most restrictive legal-gender-recognition situations. Lithuania's Civil Code grants the right to medically change gender in principle, but no legal framework regulating the procedure has existed for 17 years — a deadlock the Constitutional Court refused to resolve in September 2025, perpetuating what an ECtHR body called a "distressing legal uncertainty."
